walkthroughs.body_html:
Introduction to Business Management — a core area of Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Introduction to Business Management brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Introduction to Business Management.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

What is the difference between profit and revenue?
options: Profit and revenue are different words for the same thing.
A franchise is when employees buy shares in their company.
Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity sold); profit is revenue minus total costs — what is left after paying for everything.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
A franchise is when a business owns multiple branches itself.
A franchise is when employees buy shares in their company.
An arrangement where a franchisor grants a franchisee the right to use their brand, products and systems in exchange for fees and a share of revenue.
Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness.

mcqs.q: What is Herzberg's distinction between hygiene factors and motivators?
options: Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
Hygiene factors (pay, conditions, policies) prevent dissatisfaction when present but don't motivate; motivators (recognition, achievement, responsibility) create positive satisfaction.
Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness.
Higher pay always motivates employees.
